title: The calibration practice: rows with filters, a confidence per coordinate, items seen together to compare, relative order within a selection, going up and down; naming a cell once enough is mapped and testing against the name; cross-checking with the zodiac (3x4) and tarot (3x7, no fool) layers, the 4 and 7 mapping the same row with different valence (2026-11-07)

sections.name: narrative
sections.label: Narrative
sections.content:
Can you build me an interface for calibration.

In coda I worked through items in rows with filters. I would mark each coordinate on an axis with a confidence. I need to see them together to allow comparing.

I will not always be able to tell an axis initially. So I go up and down, working and reworking.

Sometimes I need to sort by an axis. But often not absolutely. Within a selection I may be able to say what the relative order is.

There is another level of cross check.

When I have mapped enough items, I can name a cell. Once a cell had a name and description. I can then also test against that name.

This means that I can manage the sometimes obscure phrasing of an individual item...

And then I also cross check with the zodiac .( 3x4)
And I add a tarot layer as well. (3x7 no fool)

The 4 and 7 map the same row with different Valence.

Aries ~ magician + high priestess
Taurus ~ high priestess + empress + emperor
Gemini ~ emperor + hierophant+ lovers
Cancer ~ lovers + chariot

These esoteric systems are all my own training models

sections.name: source
sections.label: Source
sections.content: The owner, in conversation with Claude Code, 2026-11-07, three messages while the owner's level rubric was being re-run on haiku and qwen; the first is a request (an interface for calibration), the rest describe the practice the interface serves; recorded verbatim. Note the cell-naming cross-check: a named cell with a description becomes a second thing to test an item against, which handles obscure phrasing.
